summary: AgroPulse is a bilingual, farmer-friendly web platform that translates open NASA satellite data (HLS v2.0, SMAP, and GPM IMERG) and USDA soil and crop datasets (SSURGO and Cropland Data Layer) into clear, actionable decisions for sustainable agriculture.   We developed an interactive decision-support tool featuring a continuous 30-meter satellite heatmap, goal-based crop rotation recommendations, a 10-year climate stress simulator, and voice-guided action plans. Behind its intuitive visual interface, AgroPulse integrates soil erosion, water balance, and multicriteria optimization models with quantified uncertainty so farmers can evaluate trade-offs without complex statistical jargon.   This project addresses the challenge of making Earth observation data accessible and practical for real-world farming. In regions like the U.S. Corn Belt, leaving fields bare over winter accelerates topsoil erosion, nitrate leaching, and summer drought vulnerability. By showing farmers exactly how cover crops and diversified rotations protect soil moisture, cut fertilizer loss, and boost long-term resilience, AgroPulse bridges the gap between space science and everyday field management.
details:
• What it does and how it works: AgroPulse is an interactive precision agriculture web platform that translates open Earth observation data into practical, field-level decisions. It works by ingesting multi-source open data—specifically NASA satellite datasets (HLS v2.0 surface reflectance, SMAP soil moisture, and GPM IMERG climate baselines) alongside USDA datasets (SSURGO soil surveys and the Cropland Data Layer)—to model a high-resolution 30-meter spatial grid of a farm field. Users can inspect local soil characteristics, choose productivity and conservation priorities, simulate 10-year predictive climate horizons through dynamic satellite views, and receive optimized crop rotation plans.
    • Programming Language: Python
    • Framework & UI: Streamlit
    • Data Processing & Scientific Computing: Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Pyarrow
    • Visualization & Mapping: Plotly, Matplotlib, Pillow
    • Infrastructure & Deployment: GitHub, Git, and Streamlit Community Cloud
  • Creativity of the project: AgroPulse stands out creatively by reimagining how complex geospatial and scientific data is communicated. Rather than overwhelming agricultural users with dense statistical jargon, confidence intervals, or technical models, it translates advanced multi-criteria decision analysis (TOPSIS), soil water balances, and spatial raster interpolations into an intuitive, farmer-friendly interface featuring a smooth continuous satellite heatmap, an interactive 10-year predictive time slider, and voice-guided briefings.
  • Factors considered by the team: The team focused heavily on user-centric design (making sure farmers with no data-science background could understand and trust the tools), regional agronomic realities (such as Iowa's corn-soybean rotation cycles and spring moisture risks), economic viability, rigorous scientific auditability (reproducibility metadata, data provenance, and transparency), and strict adherence to open-source licenses and NASA/USDA open-data citation standards.
